summary: Coppock Curve: a 10-bar weighted average of the sum of a 14-bar and an 11-bar rate of change, around zero.
overview: The Coppock Curve is a slow momentum line in its own pane. It was first made for monthly charts to spot the end of long declines.
The line and fill are green above zero and red below.
how: Coppock = WMA(ROC(source, 14) + ROC(source, 11), 10). ROC is the percent change from that many bars ago.
The original used monthly closes; here the lengths are in chart bars. Because the weighted average favors recent values, the curve turns a little sooner than a simple average would.
use: Some traders watch an upturn from below zero as a sign of recovering momentum.
Use zero-line crosses as broad momentum changes.
Use it on weekly or monthly charts as in its original design.
Compare its slope with price to see momentum fading.
alerts: Alerts: you can alert on its line crossing a value or the candle close (from the chart's + menu); checked while ZoroCharts is open.
notes: Works on any symbol and timeframe; it only needs candle data.
It is slow by design and better suited to higher timeframes.
It is not built to mark tops; its original use was spotting the end of declines.
